newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico business chief wary of PRI economy meddling.
newsitem.headline: Mexico business chief wary of PRI economy meddling.

text.p: Mexican business leader Carlos Abascal cautioned on Tuesday the government may try to use economic recovery programmes as a political tool to gain votes in the 1997 mid-term elections.
The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has been losing ground in municipal and state elections after almost seven decades of political power.

"Our business leaders will be doing a study ... to be certain the government does not use its (influence over the economy) for electoral purposes," Abascal told reporters. "It is a concern that we all share."

Abascal, who is the leader of the Mexican Employers' Confederation (Coparmex), said economic programmes in the recent accord reached between government, labour and business leaders could be manipulated to benefit the PRI. The plan calls for raising the minimum wage among other things.
